chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yāsīn al-Ḍarīr, from Ḥarīz, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
About a man who has milk with him: may he perform wudu (ablution) with it for salat (prayer)? He said:
No. It is only water and earth.
So he negated that anything other than water and earth may be used for wudu (ablution).

key_terms.الصَّعِيدُ: earth or clean ground, the valid basis for tayammum
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), for which ritual purification is required
key_terms.اللَّبَنُ: milk, mentioned here as a substance asked about for purification
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water, the valid substance for wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يَتَوَضَّأُ: to perform wudu (ablution) for ritual purification

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) be performed with milk or only with water and earth?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning ritual purification for salat (prayer). It restricts valid purification to water for wudu (ablution) and earth for tayammum, excluding other substances such as milk.
